title: JavaScript Asynchronous Programming Core Check
description: Check your understanding of asynchronous JavaScript, callbacks, promises, async/await, error handling, and parallel tasks.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What does asynchronous programming allow JavaScript to do?

options.text: Schedule work to finish later without blocking everything else

questions.explanation: Async programming lets JavaScript continue running while waiting operations finish later.

options.text: A function passed to another function to be called later
A value returned only by classes

questions.explanation: Callbacks are functions passed as arguments and invoked later by another function or API.

options.text: Deeply nested callbacks that become hard to read and maintain
A syntax error caused by arrays
A promise that resolves too quickly
An async function with no await

questions.explanation: Callback hell is nested callback-based async code that becomes difficult to follow.

options.text: A future result of an asynchronous operation

questions.explanation: A Promise represents async work that may fulfill or reject later.
A Promise starts pending, then settles as fulfilled or rejected.

questions.prompt: Which method handles a rejected Promise?
What does an `async` function always return?
questions.explanation: Async functions always return promises, even when returning a normal value.

options.text: Waits for a Promise inside an async function
Turns an array into a Set

questions.explanation: `await` pauses the async function until the awaited Promise settles.

questions.prompt: How do you commonly handle rejected promises with `async` / `await`?
questions.explanation: Rejected awaited promises throw inside the async function and can be caught with `try...catch`.

options.text: Waiting for multiple promises to fulfill together

questions.explanation: `Promise.all()` waits for all input promises and returns their resolved values in input order.

questions.prompt: What happens if one promise rejects inside `Promise.all()`?

options.text: JavaScript converts it to a callback

questions.explanation: `Promise.all()` rejects as soon as one of the input promises rejects.

questions.prompt: Which loop is usually better for sequential async work than `forEach`?
questions.explanation: `for...of` can await each iteration sequentially. `forEach` does not wait for async callbacks.
